newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ First's Peters outlines coalition boundaries.
newsitem.headline: NZ First's Peters outlines coalition boundaries.

text.p: New Zealand First leader Winston Peters on Wednesday named family, sustainable economic growth and a better political system as pivotal for a coalition deal with his party after Saturday's general election, the New Zealand Press Association reported.
He named five priorities in total, but said those three were "NZ First coalition policy".
NZ First would also demand a detailed coalition agreement, because of the track record of Labour and National, he told a lunchtime meeting in Glenfield, Auckland.
Peters said welfare and the interests of family, health and the education of children were the highest priority.
Secondly, NZ First would demand that the economy was geared for exporters and producers.
Thirdly the party would demand "some basic fairness for the political system", he said in a prepared speech.
Fourth, NZ First would demand NZ's best interests were maintained -- in terms of stopping state asset sales, controlling immigration, and stopping land sales to foreigners.
Fifth, NZ First would insist of its coalition partner that parliamentary reform was a vital ingredient in the next parliament.

Peters repeated that Labour's social agenda was closest to NZ First, but its economic policies were worrying. He said he was appalled by the lack of social agenda from the outgoing conservative Natonal Party government, and National's obsession with inflation was hampering opportunities for exporters and freezing economic growth.
Peters said demands that NZ First name its coalition partner before the election were tantamount to asking the party to be dishonest.
"Given the track record of both National and Labour, NZ First wants to have a clearly defined coalition agreement to which there is absolute commitment," he said.
